radix/corpus/operatores/modular-word-u64.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

Unsigned 64-bit modular-word arithmetic and bit-pattern edges.

# =============================================================================
# modulus<u64> — Unsigned 64-bit modular-word arithmetic and bit-pattern edges.
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Modular word contract — `modulus<u64>` wraps on overflow; demonstrates max + 1, zero - 1.
#   • Carrier-mix equality — Conversions and arithmetic results compare by value across carriers.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Assuming 64-bit modular words trap on overflow like checked numerus types.
#
# See also: numerus, ¬, ⇐, ⇒
# =============================================================================

# operatores/modular-word-u64 — modulus<u64> edge vectors
#
# MODULAR WORD CONTRACT:
#   modulus<u64> is an unsigned 64-bit modular word. Addition, subtraction,
#   multiplication, negation, bitwise operations, and shifts use u64 wrapping.
#   Division and remainder by zero fail.

main {
    var uint<u64> max ← 18446744073709551615
    const uint<u64> one ← 1
    var uint<u64> zero ← 0
    const int<u64> converted ← one ↦ int<u64>

    print max + one
    print zero - one
    print max * 2
    print -one
    print ¬zero
    print one ⇐ 64
    print max ⇒ 64
    print max > zero

    # Carrier-mix equality: conversions and arithmetic results compare by
    # value against literals (review regression).
    const uint<u64> uno ← 1 ↦ uint<u64>
    print one ≡ uno
    print one ≡ one + 0

    max ⊕
    zero ⊖
    print max
    print zero

    const uint<u64> methodSum ← max.addita(one)
    const uint<u64> methodShift ← max.sinistrata(64)
    var uint<u64> methodAcc ← 0
    methodAcc.adde(one)
    methodAcc.sinistra(64)
    print converted
    print methodSum
    print methodShift
    print methodAcc

    const list<uint<u64>> words ← [one, max]
    print words.accipe(1) coalesce (0 ∷ uint<u64>)

    var list<uint<u64>> sorted ← [18446744073709551615, 3, 10, 2]
    sorted.ordina()
    print sorted
}

18446744073709551615
